title: Game Design Concepts Atlas
description: Curriculum-focused map of mechanics, dynamics, feedback, balance, level design, accessibility, UX, playtesting and competitive viability for esports game analysis and design.

curriculumPresets.title: Full game design system
curriculumPresets.description: Explore how rules, mechanics, player behaviour, feedback and testing combine to shape playable systems.

curriculumPresets.title: L3 Unit 9: Games Design
curriculumPresets.description: Focus on mechanics, systems, balance, UX, accessibility, level design and playtesting.

nodes.name: Game Design System
nodes.note: Game design coordinates rules, mechanics, information, challenge, feedback and presentation into a coherent player experience.
nodes.hook: Pick one competitive game and trace how a single rule changes player behaviour.

nodes.name: Rules & Systems
nodes.note: Rules define what is allowed, what changes game state and what counts as success or failure.
nodes.hook: Identify one explicit rule and one emergent consequence in the same game.

nodes.name: Mechanics
nodes.note: Mechanics are actions and rule-governed interactions available to players or game systems.
nodes.hook: Separate a mechanic from an animation or visual effect.

nodes.name: Core Gameplay Loop
nodes.note: The core loop describes the repeated pattern of actions, feedback and outcomes that structures play.
nodes.hook: Write the shortest possible loop for a round of your chosen esport.

nodes.name: Resources & Economy
nodes.note: Games use limited resources such as time, health, currency, ammunition, cooldowns or positional control to force trade-offs.
nodes.hook: Find one resource whose value changes depending on game state.

nodes.name: Feedback
nodes.note: Feedback communicates the result, state or consequence of player actions through visual, audio, haptic or systemic responses.
nodes.hook: Find a moment where bad feedback could cause a correct decision to feel wrong.

nodes.name: Readability & Clarity
nodes.note: Competitive readability helps players rapidly distinguish threats, allies, objectives, effects and relevant state.
nodes.hook: Pause a chaotic team fight and identify which visual elements preserve or damage clarity.

nodes.name: Game Feel
nodes.note: Game feel describes the responsiveness and sensory quality of interaction, including timing, animation, sound and camera response.
nodes.hook: Explain how two games can implement the same mechanic but feel completely different.

nodes.name: Balance
nodes.note: Balance manages relative power, risk, reward and viable choice so that competition remains meaningful.
nodes.hook: Distinguish balanced from perfectly equal.

nodes.name: Risk & Reward
nodes.note: Risk-reward structures ask players to trade safety, resources or probability for greater potential gain.
nodes.hook: Find one play that is strong because it is risky rather than despite being risky.

nodes.name: Counterplay
nodes.note: Counterplay gives opponents meaningful ways to respond, anticipate or punish powerful actions.
nodes.hook: Choose an ability and list what information or options opponents need for fair counterplay.

nodes.name: Metagame
nodes.note: The metagame is the evolving set of dominant strategies, picks and expectations created by player adaptation around the game rules.
nodes.hook: Explain how a patch can change the metagame without changing the win condition.

nodes.name: Level & Spatial Design
nodes.note: Spatial design shapes routes, sightlines, cover, objectives, encounter timings and positional advantage.
nodes.hook: Mark three locations on a map where geometry changes tactical choice.

nodes.name: Chokepoints & Lanes
nodes.note: Restricted routes concentrate movement and interaction, creating predictable pressure points and control contests.
nodes.hook: Explain how adding one alternate route changes defender advantage.

nodes.name: Sightlines
nodes.note: Sightlines control what can be seen or threatened from a position and strongly influence range, information and exposure.
nodes.hook: Compare a long sightline and a close corner for different weapon or character archetypes.

nodes.name: User Experience & Accessibility
nodes.note: UX concerns how effectively players understand, navigate and interact with the game and its surrounding interfaces.
nodes.hook: Find a usability problem that is not part of the core gameplay challenge.

nodes.name: Onboarding
nodes.note: Onboarding introduces controls, goals and systems so that new players can form accurate mental models.
nodes.hook: Design one tutorial task that teaches by doing instead of by paragraph.

nodes.name: Accessibility
nodes.note: Accessibility reduces avoidable barriers through adaptable presentation, input, navigation and communication choices.
nodes.hook: Identify an accessibility feature that improves play without changing competitive rules.

nodes.name: Playtesting & Iteration
nodes.note: Playtesting collects evidence from actual interaction so assumptions can be challenged before changes are accepted.
nodes.hook: Write a test question that can be answered by observation rather than opinion alone.

nodes.name: Prototype
nodes.note: A prototype is a deliberately limited implementation built to answer specific design questions quickly.
nodes.hook: State what your prototype intentionally does not need to include.

nodes.name: Telemetry & Player Data
nodes.note: Telemetry records player or system behaviour to reveal patterns that may not be visible from anecdotal feedback.
nodes.hook: Choose one event worth logging and explain what decision the data could support.

nodes.name: Iteration
nodes.note: Iteration repeats design, test, evaluation and change until evidence supports a stronger solution.
nodes.hook: Show one change where fixing a problem could introduce a new one elsewhere.
